result.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
result.comment: 54 pages, 3 figures. Code and models: https://github.com/GerhardTrippen/Zugwise
result.summary: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将手写国际象棋记谱的数字化重新表述为「整局重建」而非逐格手写识别，借用国际象棋引擎的静态交换评估、牵制检测等工具判断「人类是否可能写下这步棋」，以荒谬性检测暴露「合法但错误」的静默错误，并用反向搜索把后段症状追溯到出错步，再将双方记录对齐合并、在分歧处停止并交人复核。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「静默错误只能靠跨步全局一致性暴露」「从后期症状反向定位致错步」以及「证据分歧时停止并交由人裁决」的思路，可能为 LVR 中轨迹级错误归因、证据筛选与停止决策提供可供核查的类比线索，但任务本身是符号化棋局重建与 OCR，与 VLM 内部状态表示无直接联系。
